text:
On the morning of 14 March 2031, the council chamber in the Harlow Basin was quiet in the way rooms are quiet when a long argument has finally ended. For nearly a century, engineers and ratepayers had debated whether the hills north of Dunmarrow could ever be crossed by water rather than around them.

That day, the final route was confirmed. The Dunmarrow Canal Tunnel will run 11 kilometres, according to the Dunmarrow Canal Tunnel Feasibility and Route Report (Report DWA-31/07), presented to the Harlow Basin Regional Council.

Marisol Treadgold, Chief Engineer of the Dunmarrow Waterways Authority, has described the route as the product of decades of patient surveying. The tunnel is budgeted at 2.4 billion Verrian marks, with boring planned to take six years.

It is a modest span of time, set against the long wait that preceded it.
